test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A man sells 36 bags for Rs 3600, which results in a 20% loss. How many bags must he sell for Rs 3200 to make a 60% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the unitary formula: (Price₁ / (Quantity₁ × Selling%₁)) = (Price₂ / (Quantity₂ × Selling%₂))

Here, Selling%₁ = 100 − 20 = 80 and Selling%₂ = 100 + 60 = 160

⇒ (3600 / (36 × 80)) = (3200 / (n × 160))

⇒ 100 / 80 = 20 / n

⇒ n = (20 × 80) / 100 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16 bags.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹3600 for 36 bags

Initial Loss = 20% | Target Profit = 60%

Target Selling Price (SP₂) = ₹3200

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP × [100 / (100 − Loss%)]

New SP = CP × [(100 + Profit%) / 100]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa58c9dbd6251912a728cb7b3ce17c736403acd94e100854e57f8061f98062b8.png] 

⇒ Initial SP per bag = 3600 ÷ 36 = ₹100

⇒ Cost Price (CP) per bag = 100 × (100 / 80) = ₹125

⇒ New SP per bag for 60% profit = 125 × (160 / 100) = ₹200

⇒ Number of bags for ₹3200 = 3200 ÷ 200

⇒ Number of bags = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16 bags.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage for SP

If an item is sold at multiple profit/loss stages, the final SP = CP × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100).

Marked Price and Discount

The relationship between CP and MP is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit% = [Error / (True Value − Error)] × 100 when the dealer uses a false weight.
